Main Street Capital (MAIN) recently slipped 1.01%, lagging the S&P 500, as investors turned attention to the company's August 6, 2026 earnings report and the latest expectations for profit and revenue.

See our latest analysis for Main Street Capital.

At a share price of $53.47, Main Street Capital has seen a 7.37% 1 month share price return but is down 13.41% on a year to date basis. Its 3 year total shareholder return of 60.91% and 5 year total shareholder return of 91.19% point to momentum that has cooled recently as investors reassess growth prospects and income risks ahead of the upcoming earnings release.

If the recent move in Main Street Capital has you reassessing your portfolio income ideas, it could be a good moment to broaden your search with 18 top founder-led companies

After a strong multi year run and a recent pullback, Main Street Capital now sits close to analyst targets yet still shows a sizeable intrinsic value gap. Is most of the upside already in the rear view mirror, or not?

Most Popular Narrative: 2.4% Undervalued

The most followed narrative currently values Main Street Capital at $54.80 per share compared with the last close at $53.47, implying modest upside based on detailed long term forecasts.

The analysts have a consensus price target of $54.8 for Main Street Capital based on their expectations of its future earnings growth, profit margins and other risk factors.

In order for you to agree with the analysts, you would need to believe that by 2029, revenues will be $673.9 million, earnings will be $355.0 million, and it would be trading on a PE ratio of 21.0x, assuming you use a discount rate of 9.2%.

Want to understand why Main Street Capital could justify trading above today's level? The narrative leans heavily on steadier revenue expansion, slimmer margins, and a much richer earnings multiple a few years out. Curious which assumptions really carry that fair value and how sensitive they are to small changes in growth or profitability?

Result: Fair Value of $54.80 (UNDERVALUED)

However, if credit trends worsen or supplemental dividends are cut more sharply than expected, Main Street Capital's income appeal and valuation support could come under pressure.
